The pages give no extent before 1736; the Konkan coast about Murud and Danda-Rajpuri stands in (the Peshwa took "much of the surrounding area" in 1733-1736), with Jafarabad in Kathiawar, a dependency of the Nawab (undated). Inside no Cliopatria shape.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the island with Murud and Shrivardhan; the infobox gives 839 km2 in 1931 (not counting Jafarabad), the drawn circles about 1,500 km2 (ratio 1.8, within the factor of two). How the state recovered Murud and Shrivardhan after 1745 is not on the pages.

region.text: the Siddi coast of the Konkan about Murud-Janjira, with Jafarabad

ledger.note: 1489: the Ahmadnagar admiral Piram Khan takes Murud-Janjira. Infobox "Established: 1489"; "According to legend, the Ahmadnagar Sultanate sent admiral Piram Khan ... to take Murud-Janjira from Ram Patil in 1489". The Murud-Janjira page names Itbarrao Koli as the builder of the island and dates the fort to 1567.
1733: Peshwa Bajirao attacks Janjira. "Peshwa Bajirao launched a campaign against Janjira. He took much of the surrounding area but not Janjira fort."
September 1736: peace after the Marathas beat the Siddis on 19 April 1736 near Rewas. "Peace was brokered in September 1736, but the Siddis were confined to only" Janjira, Gowalkot and Anjanvel.

ledger.note: 1745: Tulaji Angre takes Gowalkot and Anjanvel. "The forts of Gowalkot and Anjanvel were then captured by Tulaji Angre in 1745."

ledger.note: 1745: bridging, page silent. The page has "the state also included the towns of Murud and Shrivardhan" (area 839 km2 in 1931) without a date; the drawn shape from 1745 follows the loss of Gowalkot and Anjanvel and is a reading.

region.text: Janjira island with the towns of Murud and Shrivardhan, 839 km2 in 1931 without Jafarabad

ledger.note: 1948: Janjira is merged with India. "Following the independence of India in 1947, the state was merged with India" (infobox: 1948; the Murud-Janjira page: part of India after 1947).

wars.name: Maratha attacks on Janjira
wars.outcome: A Maratha assault of 10,000 men was "roundly repulsed" in 1676; Sambhaji laid siege in January 1682; Peshwa Bajirao attacked in 1733; the Marathas beat the Siddis on 19 April 1736 near Rewas; peace in September 1736 left them Janjira, Gowalkot and Anjanvel.

certainty.note: The pages give no boundaries; the Siddi coast is a reading.
The 1736 peace named the places left to the Siddis (Janjira, Gowalkot, Anjanvel); the 20th-century state had a recorded area (839 km2); the drawn circles are approximate.

notes: Two pages opened (Janjira State, Murud-Janjira). Dates conflict: 1489 (infobox, legend) against "early 1100 AD" and 1567 on the fort page. The maratha-empire dossier (sa-05-d) already records a 1736 gain from janjira-state; the Siddis served the Mughals (a 1670 transfer is not on the pages) and Bijapur before. British suzerainty 1870 ("Janjira State came under British suzerainty in 1870"): british-raj/british-empire (sa-06) should record a vassal_start. Counterparts needing dossiers: Tulaji Angre / the Angre of Kolaba, ahmadnagar-sultanate exists. Jafarabad (Kathiawar) is drawn throughout though undated. Gazetteer lacks Murud, Janjira, Gowalkot, Anjanvel, Shrivardhan, Jafarabad as places; coordinates used.
